Bank of America resumed coverage of four payroll and IT services stocks, assigning Buy ratings to Automatic Data Processing and Accenture, while initiating coverage of Paychex and Cognizant with Neutral ratings. 
Analyst Matthew O’Neill set price targets of $345 for ADP and $120 for Paychex. BofA considers ADP the more attractive investment, noting that it trades slightly below its three-year average valuation multiple despite solid growth and double-digit earnings expansion. In contrast, Paychex is becoming increasingly dependent on its Professional Employer Organization (PEO) business, which manages HR and employee benefits for small businesses, while growth in its larger core payroll division has slowed to approximately 4%. 
For Accenture, BofA established a $288 price target, arguing that AI adoption is encouraging companies to consolidate technology spending among fewer, larger service providers.

🥇 GOLD PRICE FORECASTS FOR 2027 | WHAT IS WALL STREET EXPECTING?

Major global investment banks continue to publish and revise their gold price forecasts for 2027.

Here are some of the latest projections:

• UBS: $5,000/oz
• Goldman Sachs: $4,800/oz
• Wells Fargo: $5,200–5,400/oz
• HSBC: $4,825/oz (annual average)
• Bank of America: $4,813/oz (annual average)
• Deutsche Bank: $5,100/oz
• CIBC: $5,200/oz
• JPMorgan Private Bank: $4,450–4,750/oz

What is particularly interesting is how these forecasts have changed.

Goldman Sachs lowered its year-end 2027 target from $5,400 to $4,800.

Wells Fargo revised its forecast from $5,800–6,000 to $5,200–5,400.

UBS previously projected $5,400 for September 2027, while its latest year-end target stands at $5,000.

My take:

Although several major banks have revised their short- and medium-term expectations downward, the $5,000/oz level remains firmly on the radar for 2027.

Central bank gold purchases, US real interest rates, the US dollar’s trajectory and rising global debt will remain key drivers.

Do you think gold can reach $5,000/oz by the end of 2027?
